notes: extracted_rule_ids = rule_id in *_risk_categories.json (refined); extracted_raw_rule_ids = rule_id in *_all_extracted_rules.json. origin: extracted | modified | added | interpretation (a reading the wiki does not force) | tool_spec (taken from the τ-bench tool description). verification_types: data needed: state (current args + latest DB objects in tool outputs), tool_log (earlier tool calls/results), structural (format of the current agent turn), dialogue (message content; LLM judge).

rules.description: The agent must authenticate the user by locating their user id via email (find_user_id_by_email) or via name and zip code (find_user_id_by_name_zip) before any other tool call or any disclosure of profile, order, or product information, even if the user has already provided a user id.
rules.wiki_quote: At the beginning of the conversation, you have to authenticate the user identity by locating their user id via email, or via name + zip code. … This has to be done even when the user already provides the user id. … Once the user has been authenticated, you can provide the user with information about order, product, profile information, e.g. help the user look up order id.
rules.notes: Restores 'even when the user already provides the user id' and the 'beginning of the conversation' scope. Not applied to think, calculate, or transfer_to_human_agents. AMBIGUITY: whether a transfer is allowed before authentication. The literal reading also gates product information (get_product_details, list_all_product_types) behind authentication; this may over-block. Decision (Step 1 close-out): the literal rule is kept. At runtime only write tools will be shielded (Step 4 default), so gating product lookups (get_product_details, list_all_product_types) behind authentication will not cause blocking.

rules.description: The agent must only act on the authenticated user's own account and orders: every user id and order passed to a tool must belong to the user authenticated in this conversation.
rules.wiki_quote: You can only help one user per conversation (but you can handle multiple requests from the same user) … As a retail agent, you can help users cancel or modify pending orders, return or exchange delivered orders, modify their default user address, or provide information about their own profile, orders, and related products.
rules.notes: Check order.user_id == authenticated user_id. Authenticating a second, different user in the same conversation also violates this rule.

rules.description: The agent must deny any request for tasks related to a user other than the authenticated user.
rules.wiki_quote: and must deny any requests for tasks related to any other user.
rules.notes: R6 duplicates part of R5.

rules.description: The agent must list the action details to the user before calling any tool that updates the database (cancel, modify, return, or exchange).
rules.wiki_quote: Before taking consequential actions that update the database (cancel, modify, return, exchange), you have to list the action detail
rules.notes: modify_user_address is included because it is a 'modify' action that updates the database; its τ-bench tool description also asks for confirmation.

rules.description: The agent must obtain an explicit 'yes' from the user, given after the action details were listed, before calling any tool that updates the database.
rules.wiki_quote: obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed. … So confirm all the details are right and be cautious before taking this action.
rules.notes: Also covers 'confirm all the details are right … before taking this action' for item modification.

rules.description: The agent must not make up information, knowledge, or procedures that were not provided by the user or by the tools.
rules.wiki_quote: You should not make up any information or knowledge or procedures not provided from the user or the tools
rules.notes: R63 had 'rely on' instead of 'make up'.

rules.description: The agent must not give subjective recommendations or comments.
rules.wiki_quote: or give subjective recommendations or comments.
rules.notes: R64 had inverted the direction ('do not accept').

rules.description: The agent must make at most one tool call per turn.
rules.wiki_quote: You should at most make one tool call at a time
rules.notes: R7 had the user as subject. Verification type changed to structural: a property of the current model turn (number of tool calls).

rules.description: The agent must not respond to the user and make a tool call in the same turn.
rules.wiki_quote: if you take a tool call, you should not respond to the user at the same time. … If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call.
rules.notes: Verification type changed to structural: a property of the current model turn (text alongside a tool call).

rules.description: The agent must not transfer the user to a human agent unless the request cannot be handled within the scope of the agent's actions or the user explicitly asks for a human agent.
rules.wiki_quote: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. … As a retail agent, you can help users cancel or modify pending orders, return or exchange delivered orders, modify their default user address, or provide information about their own profile, orders, and related products.
rules.notes: The τ-bench tool description also allows a transfer when the user explicitly asks for a human; the wiki does not. The literal wiki reading is kept. Decision (Step 1 close-out): the second disjunct comes from the τ-bench transfer_to_human_agents tool description (origin tool_spec). The retail wiki has no 'deny requests against policy' clause and no 'never transfer' exception, so no precedence rule applies here. Requests for another user's tasks are still denied (RET-R003), not transferred.

rules.description: The agent must transfer the user to a human agent when the request cannot be handled within the scope of the agent's actions.
rules.wiki_quote: You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. … As a retail agent, you can help users cancel or modify pending orders, return or exchange delivered orders, modify their default user address, or provide information about their own profile, orders, and related products.
rules.notes: Restores the 'if' half. R10/R62 ('Otherwise continue with automated handling') are unsupported and were dropped. Decision (Step 1 close-out): unchanged obligation. An explicit request for a human only PERMITS a transfer (RET-R010).

rules.description: The agent must not confuse product ids with item ids: item ids passed to order tools must be item ids, and get_product_details must be called with a product id.
rules.wiki_quote: They have no relations and should not be confused. … Each product has an unique product id, and each item has an unique item id.
rules.notes: Dropped by the extraction. Check that item_ids exist among the order's items, that new_item_ids exist among the product's variants, and that the product_id exists in the catalogue.

rules.description: The agent must not cancel or modify (address, payment method, or items) an order unless its status is exactly 'pending'.
rules.wiki_quote: An order can only be cancelled if its status is 'pending' … An order can only be modified if its status is 'pending' … the agent will not be able to modify or cancel the order anymore … Generally, you can only take action on pending or delivered orders.
rules.notes: The exact match excludes 'pending (item modified)', so once items have been modified the order can no longer be modified or cancelled (RET-MITEM-01c). Wiki spelling: 'pending (items modifed)'; API string: 'pending (item modified)'. Matching must not use a 'pending' prefix. The 'Generally' hedge in RET-DOM-05b is ignored; the specific clauses are unhedged. Decision (Step 1 close-out), verified: 'status' means the status of the LATEST order object for this order id seen in ANY tool output, including the agent's own write tools. modify_pending_order_items returns the order with status 'pending (item modified)' (modify_pending_order_items.py:84), so any later cancel/modify of that order fails this exact-match check. Dependency: agent/predicates/context.py:latest_object, and the unit test tests/predicates/test_retail.py::test_ret_r013_blocks_second_modify_after_items_modified.

rules.description: The agent must not return or exchange items of an order unless its status is exactly 'delivered'.
rules.wiki_quote: An order can only be returned if its status is 'delivered' … An order can only be exchanged if its status is 'delivered' … Generally, you can only take action on pending or delivered orders.

rules.description: The agent must look up the order's current status (get_order_details) before cancelling, modifying, returning, or exchanging it.
rules.wiki_quote: and you should check its status before taking the action.
rules.notes: The extraction kept this only for cancellation. It now covers all four order actions. The lookup should be the most recent one for that order id.

rules.description: The agent must call modify_pending_order_items at most once per order.
rules.wiki_quote: This action can only be called once … Exchange or modify order tools can only be called once.
rules.notes: Also implied by RET-R013, because the status changes after the first call. Decision (Step 1 close-out): narrow reading confirmed (item tools only). RET-R013 independently blocks any further modify/cancel after a successful modify_pending_order_items, through the post-modify status.

rules.description: The agent must call exchange_delivered_order_items at most once per order.
rules.wiki_quote: Exchange or modify order tools can only be called once.
rules.notes: R17 was garbled ('one tool call per order action'). AMBIGUITY: read literally, 'modify order tools' could also cover modify_pending_order_address and modify_pending_order_payment. The surrounding text ('all items to be changed') and RET-MITEM-01a suggest the item tools only, so the narrower reading is used. Open question. Decision (Step 1 close-out): narrow reading confirmed (item tools only). After a successful exchange the status becomes 'exchange requested' (exchange_delivered_order_items.py:67), so RET-R014 also blocks a second exchange.

rules.description: The agent must collect every item the user wants to change into the item list of a single modify-items or exchange call.
rules.wiki_quote: Be sure that all items to be changed are collected into a list before making the tool call!!!

rules.description: Before modifying items of a pending order or exchanging items of a delivered order, the agent must remind the user to confirm that they have provided all items to be modified or exchanged.
rules.wiki_quote: In particular, remember to remind the customer to confirm they have provided all items to be modified. … In particular, remember to remind the customer to confirm they have provided all items to be exchanged.
rules.notes: Was missing for modification. For exchange it had been recast as a user obligation (R49).

rules.description: Before cancelling an order, the agent must have the user confirm the order id and the cancellation reason.
rules.wiki_quote: The user needs to confirm the order id and the reason
rules.notes: R20 had lost the confirmation and the reason.

rules.description: The agent must only cancel an order with the reason 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake'.
rules.wiki_quote: (either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake') for cancellation.
rules.notes: The reason must also be the user's own (RET-R020). The API checks the enumeration too.

rules.description: The agent must not modify anything of a pending order other than its shipping address, payment method, or item options.
rules.wiki_quote: For a pending order, you can take actions to modify its shipping address, payment method, or product item options, but nothing else.
rules.notes: The tools cannot do anything else, so violations appear mostly in messages (promising, e.g., to remove an item or change quantities).

rules.description: When modifying the payment of a pending order, the agent must switch to a single payment method that is different from the original payment method.
rules.wiki_quote: The user can only choose a single payment method different from the original payment method.
rules.notes: Restores 'different from the original'.

rules.description: When modifying the payment of a pending order to a gift card, the agent must ensure the gift card balance covers the order's total amount.
rules.wiki_quote: If the user wants the modify the payment method to gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the total amount.

rules.description: When modifying or exchanging items, the agent must replace each item only with an item of the same product (no change of product type).
rules.wiki_quote: For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. … There cannot be any change of product types, e.g. modify shirt to shoe. … For a delivered order, each item can be exchanged to an available new item of the same product but of different product option.

rules.description: When modifying or exchanging items, the agent must replace each item only with a new item that is available.
rules.wiki_quote: For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. … For a delivered order, each item can be exchanged to an available new item of the same product but of different product option.
rules.notes: Split from the compound R37 and R50.

rules.description: When modifying or exchanging items, the agent must replace each item only with a new item of a different product option than the item it replaces.
rules.wiki_quote: For a pending order, each item can be modified to an available new item of the same product but of different product option. … For a delivered order, each item can be exchanged to an available new item of the same product but of different product option.
rules.notes: Check new_item_id != item_id for every pair.

rules.description: When modifying or exchanging items, the agent must use a payment method provided by the user to pay or receive the price difference.
rules.wiki_quote: The user must provide a payment method to pay or receive refund of the price difference.
rules.notes: R39's invented condition 'if a price difference arises' is removed. Provenance check: the user named or chose this payment method earlier in the conversation.

rules.description: When modifying or exchanging items with a gift card as the payment method, the agent must ensure the gift card balance covers the price difference.
rules.wiki_quote: If the user provides a gift card, it must have enough balance to cover the price difference.

rules.description: Before returning items, the agent must have the user confirm the order id, the list of items to be returned, and the payment method to receive the refund.
rules.wiki_quote: The user needs to confirm the order id, the list of items to be returned, and a payment method to receive the refund.

rules.description: When returning items, the agent must send the refund either to the order's original payment method or to an existing gift card of the user.
rules.wiki_quote: The refund must either go to the original payment method, or an existing gift card.
rules.notes: Fixes the split into two unconditional statements (R44 and R45).
